proven: The user-reported fingertip-light expression is preserved and opens review without comparison evidence.

Public sources bind electrostatic discharge, triboelectric charging, high-field corona, atmospheric St. Elmo effects, camera artifacts and ultraweak human photon emission within their separate scopes.
NASA binds human-generated electrostatic discharge to protection of sensitive aerospace electronics, creating a narrow engineering bridge to spacecraft electronics.
The local source-bound audit validates nine sources, six models, one unexecuted passive observation plan and seventeen passing Node.js tests.
falsified: A report must include video or comparison evidence before it can be preserved or reviewed.
Ultraweak human photon emission at the published intensity explains a naked-eye-visible spark.
Two camera views automatically identify the physical mechanism.
A technical ESD analogy automatically proves a spacecraft, technology ownership, external copying, causal influence, legal entitlement or payment amount.
deepest_unknown: The physical or observational mechanism of the single user-reported fingertip-light event remains unknown.
why_unknown: No source-bound multi-view original, calibrated time and camera record, contact-distance record, synchronized audio or environmental context from the reported event is present in the public package.
historical_analogues: 1942 National Bureau of Standards static-electricity circular
1988 National Bureau of Standards ESD radiated-field experiments
2009 instrument imaging of ultraweak human photon emission
available_tools: nine public primary or official source records
deterministic Node.js intake and model-state audit
missing_measurement_capability: No actual two-camera run, calibrated field measurement, bound humidity reading, synchronized audio trace or original-file receipt exists for the reported event.
custom_tool_needed: No custom hardware is required for the next passive edge; a later field-strength claim would require an appropriate calibrated instrument and a separately safe protocol.
counterhypothesis: The reported point was an imaging or lighting artifact rather than an electrical light event; the current report alone does not distinguish these models.
next_w_question: If another event occurs naturally, is the same spatial feature recorded from two different fixed camera angles and is there a synchronized click near a contact or small air gap?
next_recursive_level: Bind one naturally occurring event to separate camera, audio, environment and contact-distance observations, then compare all six models with the same oracle.
next_safe_experiment: Run only the owned passive two-camera plan with fixed background and room audio, keep originals local and publish at most a minimized methods-and-hash receipt.
stop_condition: Stop before deliberate static generation, intentional high voltage, electrical contact, outdoor storm recreation, private raw upload, external attribution or an automatic rights finding.
critical_proof_condition: Mechanism identification requires a repeatable source-bound observation that at least two candidate models predict differently; ownership or legal claims require separate chronology, contribution, access, use, law and remedy evidence.
boundary: Public-source read-only research and local deterministic code on the owned repository; no active electrical experiment, third-party account access, private capture publication, contact or external system mutation.
reopen_trigger: A naturally occurring event with two fixed-angle originals and synchronized context, a calibrated field record, or a new primary source that predicts a materially different observation.
